newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa June reserves below market expectations.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa June reserves below market expectations.

text.p: South Africa's gold and foreign exchange reserves disappointed economists on Tuesday by coming in at the lower end of expectations.

The data provided a sobering end to a day which marked the relaxation of exchange controls allowing South African individuals to invest offshore for the first time, and which confounded pessimists predictions of a run on the rand.
The Reserve Bank said its holdings of gross gold and foreign exchange reserves rose 300 million rand to 22.1 billion rand in June from 21.8 billion rand in May.
Economists polled ahead of the figure expected reserves to rise to between 23 and 28 billion rand, with consensus at 24.68 billion rand.
Barnard Jacobs Mellet economist Chantal Friedman noted that the latest data had come off a high base in May when reserves rose 7.41 billion rand.
"But with the fact that we had such strong purchases of bonds and equities and the proceeds of the Samurai issue, the figure is not as good as one would have thought," Friedman said.

The bank said that during the month, identifiable outflows for the quarter-end June were in excess of 2.2 billion rand, while the proceeds of the government's 1.58 billion rand Samurai issue accrued to the reserves during the month.
Friedman said that excluding the central bank's second installment on the IMF Compensatory Financing Facility of 465.4 million rand, the remaining outflows could be linked to the current account.
"Presumably what they mean is that the other 1.7 billion rand is actually current account quarter-end flows," she said.

Equisec economist Dawie Roodt said that while the latest figure was slightly disappointing, the inclusion of the proceeds of the government's 2.2 billion rand Yankee issue in July gave a healthier underlying picture.

"I think it is a bit disappointing for the markets and they might tick up a couple of points. But the underlying picture is quite good. With the Yankee the reserves will be around 25 billion rand," Roodt said.
Friedman added that the latest figure was unlikely to have any impact on the interest rate outlook.
"Reserves are still up. There might be another disappinting figure in July and August, but they are still way above where they were at the end of last year."
Reserves stood at 10.31 billion rand at the end of last year.
Economists expect at least one interest rate cut in the second half of this year as the economy cools and inflation is brought under control.
